newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher, supported by Astra.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher, supported by Astra.

text.p: Swedish shares came off day lows to close higher on Thursday, supported by a rebound in drugs major Astra.
Stockholm general index ended up 0.34 percent at 2,646.65 in fairly light turnover of 3.63 billion crowns.
"It was a little more trading oriented today, with a couple of news items having some effect," a dealer said.
Astra jumped six crowns to 347.5 in a recovery after dropping eight a day earlier on its U.S. partner Merck being downgraded.
Automotive group Volvo gained five crowns to 196.
Dealers could not quite explain Volvo's strong performance, but mentioned favourable international media reports, a rebound after recent falls and a strong start for car shares on Wall Street.
Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz surged 48 crowns to 1,048 after saying first quarter sales rose 30 percent and that the sales and earnings trend remained positive.

The forestry sector fell 2.28 percent, partly as SCA's head said he did not think fine paper prices could be raised as planned this spring. Both MoDo and AssiDoman were, however, trading ex-dividend, pulling the sector index lower.
SCA slipped two to 160.5 and Stora fell one to 100.5.
MoDo dropped 12 to 213.5 crowns but was trading without a nine crown dividend and AssiDoman fell 6.5 to 192 with a dividend of 5.25 crowns being taken on Thursday.
